column3: ci_wait ignored a failed gh run watch (network timeout) and printed passed from the next gh read without saying the watch had failed; the v0.15.0 run did pass, so a gh error could sit one step from a release.
column6: tests/release.test.sh release.sh: a failing gh run watch, then GitHub reporting completed and success, passes and says the watch failed

column3: replay-faults.sh had no time limit on a check run or on a replay session, so one hung run held the whole replay forever: on 2026-09-29 a replay of this branch's faults ran 7 h 23 min in replay-baseline-per-job, whose own test had blocked writing to a named pipe that nothing read, until the person stopped it; the 13 other faults had finished in 247 to 333 seconds. The first limit sent only SIGTERM, which a run can outlive: in an 8-fault replay the baseline passed its 948.1-second limit and ended only at 1615.1 seconds; a stopped run is now force-killed (SIGKILL to its process group) when a 10-second grace period ends.
column6: tests/replay-faults.test.sh replay-faults: a hanging check is stopped at its time limit and reported TIMEOUT; the others still get verdicts

column3: The harness had no shared hard time limit or cleanup for its long-running processes. The Stop hook ran the check under Claude Code's 300-second hook timeout with no limit of its own, and a hook that times out decides nothing (research/02-claude-features.md), so a check slower than 300 s let Claude stop unchecked (fail open); harness-kit's check took 316 s in the 2026-09-29 replay. The check in land.sh, ship.sh and release.sh, the reviewer runs of review.sh and eval-reviewer.sh, gh run watch and every gh read in ship.sh and release.sh, git push, fetch and ls-remote (a push needing a password waited at its prompt), and upgrade.sh's plugin commands had no limit; upgrade.sh and predeploy-gate.mjs stopped only the first process, not its group; Claude could start a background command with no limit; and a forced kill left process groups, worktrees and temporary folders behind.
column6: tests/stop-gate.test.sh stop-gate: a check that runs past its limit blocks the stop with TIMEOUT, and its process group is gone
